heroHeadline: IFT-13 WINDOW OPENS MAY 29: Modified Suborbital Profile Expected After Booster 19 Loss — Orbital Propellant Transfer Demo Slips Past June 2026
heroSubtitle: May 25: SpaceX's IFT-13 (Ship 40 + Booster 20, Starship V3) has an FCC Special Temporary Authority window opening May 29, 2026. Following Booster 19's boostback failure on IFT-12 (May 22), industry tracking indicates IFT-13 will fly a modified suborbital profile to re-validate boostback and landing sequences before attempting orbital flight — the FAA IFT-12 mishap assessment (expected June 2026) must be resolved first. This pushes the earliest IFT-13 launch to Q3 2026 and slips the orbital propellant transfer demonstration — a NASA prerequisite for Starship HLS qualification — from a June 2026 target to Q3-Q4 2026 at minimum. A May 24 Motley Fool analysis flagged that Rocket Lab may now demonstrate orbital in-space fueling before SpaceX. In parallel, two NASA leadership milestones this week: Matt Anderson sworn in as NASA's 16th Deputy Administrator (May 21) and NASA announced an agencywide realignment to accelerate mission delivery (May 22). A NASA Moon Base strategy news conference is scheduled for May 26 at 2 PM EDT, expected to detail the $20B, 7-year lunar surface base program replacing Gateway. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 45 post-splashdown at Johnson Space Center continuing reconditioning. Artemis III structural spacer fabrication is underway at Marshall Space Flight Center; sole remaining ICPS reserved for Artemis IV (first crewed lunar landing, ~2028).
